findings.text: The first lines tell a newcomer what Athena is and that this page is a study of another project, firstmate. The first screen answers "what is this?" well.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository.

findings.text: This page lives at Athena's own address, but almost all of it is about firstmate. Someone who came to learn about Athena gets two paragraphs on Athena and then about 40 claims about another tool. That gap can confuse a newcomer about which project the site is for.

The header links to a Next steps section, which links to both GitHub repositories. A newcomer can find what to do next straight away. Installing Athena is only a link, with no command or short instructions on the page.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself

findings.text: The opening promises that Athena shows how it read the request, which models did the work and what each step cost. This page shows none of that, so a newcomer sees nothing that backs up those claims about Athena.
findings.source: It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: Defining key terms such as captain, yolo, green and red before using them helps a newcomer. But "open captain call", "merge authority", "endpoint", "durable record" and "wake" are used without definitions, and "captain call" has no Glossary entry.
The transition cards are dense and full of edge cases. A newcomer is likely to get lost here. The short overview in Start here is the part they can actually use.
findings.source: t8 in-flight → in-flight: "A ship or scout keeps its recorded harness and needs a note; a secondmate re-reads its pin and needs none, and a secondmate with no endpoint is recovered by the spawn script instead."

findings.text: Every statement links to a claim, and every claim links to exact lines at a fixed commit. This shows why the study can be trusted, and the third Next steps item explains how to check a statement.
findings.source: Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end.

findings.text: The findings are numbered f1, f3 and f4, with no f2. A newcomer may wonder whether something is missing. The section is honest that nothing was run ("every claim is marked read"), which helps a reader judge how much to trust it.
findings.source: Limits of this study — f1, f3, f4

findings.text: This sentence about where the deciders are explained is unclear: the definitions come after the section intro and before the cards, not under any cards heading. It's minor, but it makes the reader stop and look.
findings.source: The two deciders are explained below the cards' heading.
